title: HE DID AS THE LORD DIRECTED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua did to them as the Lord had directed: He hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots - Josh 11:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This short verse is easy to skim, but it carries the whole weight of Joshua's character. God gave an unusual, even costly, command — cripple the horses, burn the chariots — and Joshua did exactly that. He did not keep a few of the best chariots "just in case." He did not improve on the instructions. He simply did as the Lord had directed.

There is quiet greatness in that. Partial obedience often looks reasonable to us. Surely a few chariots would be useful later? But Joshua understood that when God speaks clearly, our job is not to negotiate but to obey. Later in Israel's history, King Saul would keep back the best of what God told him to destroy, and it cost him the kingdom (1 Sam 15). The difference between the two men is right here in this verse.

For us, the temptation is rarely to reject God outright. It is to obey ninety percent and quietly hold back the ten percent that costs us most. But Jesus, our greater Joshua, obeyed His Father completely, even to the cross (Phil 2:8). His perfect obedience covers our failures and, by His Spirit, reshapes us into people who can say with growing honesty: I did as the Lord directed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where are you tempted to hold back the costly ten percent?
- What "chariot" might God be asking you to release rather than keep?
- How does Christ's complete obedience encourage you to trust and obey?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from partial obedience that quietly protects what You have asked me to release. Thank You that Christ obeyed fully in my place. Amen.
